source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Repeat intramuscular epinephrine per protocol when anaphylaxis persists or recurs","B":"Avoid all additional epinephrine after the first intramuscular dose is administered","C":"Wait at least one hour before giving any further treatment for persistent symptoms","D":"Use an oral antihistamine alone instead of repeating epinephrine for ongoing symptoms"}}
source_row.rationale: If symptoms of anaphylaxis do not adequately improve after an initial dose of epinephrine, current guidelines support administering a repeat dose (commonly after about 5-15 minutes, per protocol) since a single dose may be insufficient, particularly in severe reactions, and this should not be delayed by relying on antihistamines or other adjunct treatments alone.
source_row.source_detail: Management section: repeat intramuscular epinephrine for persistent symptoms at guideline intervals; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: A client with anaphylaxis receives an initial dose of intramuscular epinephrine, but symptoms do not adequately improve after several minutes, and a new team member assumes no more epinephrine can be given no matter what. The nurse should instead anticipate:
